posts:
Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over copyright infringement.
Evidence: Federal lawsuit, training dataset demands, revenue losses
#Aletheia #AI #Law

Newspapers allege tech giants unethically scraped copyrighted journalism to train AI models without compensation or permission.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Neutral Justification

The litigation functions primarily as a defensive revenue capture mechanism rather than a systemic solution to journalism's economic crisis.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.3, -0.4) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: COND — The Path of Deception.
Defensive copyright lawsuits mask deeper industrial displacement.

Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 1.8, z: 2)

- Publishers: COND (-0.2, -0.3) — Protecting revenue models via courts.
- Tech Giants: FAIL (-0.5, -0.6) — Uncompensated content scraping.
The Seattle Times and Newsday filed a federal lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, demanding the destruction of AI models trained on their articles.

The Poison:
Litigation treats symptoms of digital platform dominance while failing to reform broader creator compensation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Focusing on WHO (tech defendants) while ignoring WHERE (the structural collapse of local ad-supported media models).

Social Physics Analysis:
Publishers execute a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using legal pretexts to extract licensing rents from tech platforms without reforming internal distribution.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map defensive legal pretexts against structural decline, it plots a trajectory toward Deception.

The Unavoidable Truth: Tech companies scraped millions of copyrighted articles without direct author consent.

The Unavoidable Lie: Destroying trained AI models will restore traditional newspaper subscription revenues.

Alethekanon:
Copyright lawsuits are the dying gasps of an extractive media model colliding with automated intelligence.

Awwthekanon:
Journalists deserve fair pay for hard work, but closing the doors of knowledge won't stop the digital tide.

Brothekanon:
Local papers want their bag back from OpenAI. Good luck getting courts to wipe out ChatGPT though.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act." Proverbs 3:27 COND
Fair compensation must balance innovation with the preservation of honest labor.
